Lesson 52 · A pretty carpet
Skim · 2 min

Read fast. One question.

2:00
Q1Why does the sister call the floor "a pretty carpet"?
Because the books cover every inch of the floor – they look like a colourful carpet. She is joking: the room is a mess, but she pretends to admire it.

Grammar focus

"I have been working all morning."

Drag the clock. Watch what happens to the sentence when the action is still going on – and when it is finished.

Time-lapse

8:00
Right. Books first.
🧍
8:009:0010:0011:00NOW 12:00
At 8:00 he starts working.

HAVE BEEN DOING

The action started in the past and is still going on – or has only just stopped. We care about how long.
I have been working all morning.

HAVE DONE

The action is finished. We care about the result now.
We have moved into a new house.

Still going, or finished?

Lesson 52 · A pretty carpet
Reading between the lines

Why is it funny?

The sister says three things. None of them means what it says. Click each line to go one layer deeper.

Three layers

LAYER 1 · WHAT SHE SAYS"This is the prettiest carpet I have ever seen."
What she means: "Your floor is a disaster." Saying the opposite of what you mean = irony. The clue is the exaggeration: prettiest … ever.
LAYER 2 · THE ADVICE"You don't need bookcases at all."
She has just carried a heavy bookcase up the stairs for him. Now she says he doesn't need it. The "advice" is a tease, not a solution.
LAYER 3 · THE PUNCHLINE"…sit here in your spare time and read the carpet!"
A pun: you read books, you sit on carpets – here you can do both. The joke works because the carpet really is made of books. Note the timing: she gazed at it for some time, then added – the pause makes the punchline land.

Your turn: compliment a mess

"This is the prettiest carpet I have ever seen!"

Pick a mess, make the "compliment", then add a punchline like the sister's. Gaze at it first – timing matters.

Lesson 52 · A pretty carpet
Retell · read the carpet

Now you read the carpet

Twelve books on the floor, one word each. Flip a book, say its sentence, move to the next – and you have retold the story.

How to play

Round 1: in order, one book each. Round 2: shuffle – whoever gets the book must say its sentence and the one before it.

Start: We have just moved into…
Problem: This hasn't been easy because…
Worse: To make matters worse, …
Turn: A short while ago, my sister…
End: "This is the prettiest …"
Lesson 52 · A pretty carpet
Wrap-up

Why "A pretty carpet"?

Discuss · 3 min

"You can sit here in your spare time and read the carpet!"
  • Is the sister being kind, unkind, or both? Find one word in the text that shows she is not really angry.
  • The writer says I have been working hard all morning. Has he actually achieved anything? Which sentence tells you?
  • What would you say if you walked into this room?

Homework

  • Write the sister's version of the story in 60–80 words: "I had just carried a bookcase upstairs when…"
  • Five true sentences about today with have been + -ing and a time phrase (all day, for two hours, since lunch).
  • Write one ironic "compliment" for a mess at home – and the reply.
Look at the picture. What do you think it means? Guess in English!
